verification.note: Citation (volume, issue, season and pages) checked in Sangster’s 2011 notes; the double issue is dated Fall 1996 there and April 1996 in Crossref. Text not read (the York journal site blocks automated access). Described only as a defence of gender history against Sangster’s dichotomy (Q36); the respondents’ theoretical positions are not characterised. Checked against: Sangster’s own bibliography and notes in Through Feminist Eyes (AU Press, 2011), read at https://read.aupress.ca/read/through-feminist-eyes/section/ae126747-ec01-4cc4-aeee-9e4bf07caa1e and the introduction (note 133); Crossref DOI record (no pages); answers/verification.json Q36. Addendum 2026-10-14: Addendum 2026-10-14 (Claude, Parr draft): read in full in an Internet Archive capture (15 February 2020) of the journal PDF (article/download/6970/6154). Pages 239–48 by running head. In n. 2 (p. 240) she quotes Parr's 'Gender History and Historical Practice' (in Parr and Rosenfeld, eds., Gender and History in Canada, 1996, p. 11) and says it tends 'to locate critics of gender history, feminist and anti-feminist alike, in the same oppositional group'. In n. 3 (p. 240) she notes she was reproached for not offering 'more criticism of historians such as Mariana Valverde and Joy Parr'. On p. 244 she quotes Parr (p. 14) that the move to gender 'began from the post-structuralist premise that identities were made in relationships', adding that the two 'have blossomed in tandem'. She concedes she had 'congealed and possibly blurred two issues' (p. 244). She questions 'the prevailing assumption that gender history as the field, post-structuralism as the method, equals a superior, more broad-minded history' (p. 246; n. 14 cites Parr p. 21).
